title: Start of shift at the BMC
summary: The full handover routine for an incoming monitoring officer, from logbook to rack checks.

steps.title: Sign the shift logbook
steps.detail: Record your name, staff ID and shift code (A/B/C) in the physical logbook at the console desk. Note the exact takeover time.

steps.title: Take the verbal handover brief
steps.detail: The outgoing officer walks you through open incidents, stations flagged overnight, and any equipment behaving abnormally. Do not let them leave before this brief.

steps.title: Review the previous shift's incident log
steps.detail: Open the incident register and read every entry from the last 8 hours. Flag anything marked UNRESOLVED for follow-up in your shift.

steps.title: Verify the monitoring rack status
steps.detail: Walk the rack: all receivers powered, no red LEDs, antenna switch positions matching the assignment sheet. Log any deviation immediately.

steps.title: Check the recording servers
steps.detail: Confirm both logging servers show green in the dashboard and free storage is above 15%. If storage is low, escalate to the Head of BMC before purging anything.

steps.title: Spot-check spectrum analyser calibration
steps.detail: Tune to the 100.0 MHz reference carrier and confirm level reads within ±2 dB of the calibration sheet value taped to the analyser.

steps.title: Confirm your channel assignments
steps.detail: Check the duty roster for the FM/TV channels assigned to your seat this shift and load the matching preset bank on your receiver.

steps.title: Post your on-duty status
steps.detail: Update the duty board and the group channel so the Head of BMC and the standby engineer know who holds the console.

title: Logging an interference complaint
summary: How to capture, verify and register a reported case of harmful interference.

steps.title: Capture the complaint details
steps.detail: Record the complainant, affected frequency, location, and time first observed. Use the standard intake form — never loose notes.

steps.title: Verify on the monitoring receivers
steps.detail: Tune to the affected frequency and attempt to observe the interference yourself. Save an IQ recording and a spectrum screenshot as evidence.

steps.title: Classify the interference
steps.detail: Mark it co-channel, adjacent-channel, spurious, or intermodulation based on what you observe. When unsure, mark UNCLASSIFIED and note why.

steps.title: Open an incident in the register
steps.detail: Assign the next incident number in the format BMC-INT-YYYY-###. Attach the recording and screenshot.

steps.title: Notify the Head of BMC
steps.detail: Any confirmed harmful interference is escalated the same shift — do not hold it for the morning brief.

steps.title: Schedule a direction-finding run if unresolved
steps.detail: If the source is not obvious, request a mobile DF unit through the Head of BMC and log the request number against the incident.

title: Adding a new FM station to the register
summary: Registering a newly authorised FM station so it enters monitoring and compliance cycles.

steps.title: Confirm the authorisation is signed
steps.detail: Locate the signed Frequency Authorisation letter in the records system. No register entry is created from a draft or offer letter.

steps.title: Create the station record
steps.detail: Enter call sign, assigned frequency, licensed ERP, transmitter site coordinates, and licensee details exactly as they appear on the authorisation.

steps.title: Attach the technical parameters
steps.detail: Upload the approved antenna pattern, height above average terrain, and transmitter type-approval reference.

steps.title: Set the compliance schedule
steps.detail: New stations get a first compliance measurement within 90 days of on-air date. Add it to the inspection calendar.

steps.title: Notify the BMC
steps.detail: Send the station record link to the BMC so the frequency is added to the monitoring preset banks before the on-air date.

steps.title: Confirm the register entry
steps.detail: Have a second officer verify the entry against the authorisation letter and countersign the register log.

title: Registering a new ISP or network operator
summary: Processing a new Internet Service Provider from application to entry in the operator register.

steps.title: Check the application pack is complete
steps.detail: Business registration certificate, tax clearance, network architecture description, and proof of application fee. Return incomplete packs within 5 working days.

steps.title: Review the technical plan
steps.detail: Verify the proposed spectrum use, interconnection points, and coverage plan are consistent with the licence class applied for.

steps.title: Run the due-diligence checks
steps.detail: Confirm directors against the sanctions and prior-revocation lists. Record the check date in the file.

steps.title: Draft the evaluation memo
steps.detail: Summarise findings and a clear recommendation. The memo goes to the Head of Mobile & Wireless for review before Director level.

steps.title: Route for approval
steps.detail: Approval chain: Head of Mobile & Wireless → Deputy Director, Engineering → Director, Engineering. Track it in the approvals register.

steps.title: Issue the registration and enter the register
steps.detail: On approval, generate the registration number in the format NCA/ISP/YYYY/### and create the operator record with all licence conditions attached.

title: Processing an earth station licence application
summary: From application receipt to coordination check and licence offer for a new earth station.

steps.title: Log the application
steps.detail: Assign a file number in the format NCA/SAT/ES/YYYY/### and acknowledge receipt to the applicant within 3 working days.

steps.title: Validate the technical annex
steps.detail: Check antenna diameter, transmit/receive frequencies, EIRP, and the target satellite's orbital slot against the ITU filing.

steps.title: Run the domestic coordination check
steps.detail: Screen the proposed frequencies against terrestrial fixed links and other earth stations within the coordination contour.

steps.title: Request clarifications if needed
steps.detail: All technical queries go in a single consolidated letter — avoid piecemeal back-and-forth with the applicant.

steps.title: Prepare the licence offer
steps.detail: Draft the Earth Station Licence Offer using the standard template, including all coordination conditions.

steps.title: Route to the Director General
steps.detail: Earth station licence offers are signed at DG level. Route through Director, Engineering with the coordination report attached.

title: Preparing a quarterly QoS drive test
summary: Planning and equipment checks before a quality-of-service drive test campaign.

steps.title: Confirm the route plan
steps.detail: Use the approved quarterly route set. Any route change needs sign-off from the Head of Mobile & Wireless before the campaign starts.

steps.title: Reserve the drive test vehicle and kit
steps.detail: Book the vehicle, scanner, and test handsets at least one week ahead. Confirm SIMs for all operators under test are active.

steps.title: Calibrate the measurement kit
steps.detail: Run the pre-campaign calibration script and file the calibration report — results without it are not admissible in enforcement.

steps.title: Notify operators of the campaign window
steps.detail: Send the standard notification letter giving the campaign window, but never the exact routes or dates.

steps.title: Brief the field team
steps.detail: Cover safety, logging discipline, and what counts as an anomaly worth a manual marker during the drive.
